title: UI: one Settings window for the per-user display and graphics settings

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:ui
labels.description: User interface and picking

labels.name: effort:medium
labels.description: One module or crate, a known pattern (issue-worker-medium)

labels.name: P6
labels.description: Accepted enhancement, not scheduled

body:
## Problem

The display and graphics settings are in places that their names do not explain:

- The **Theme** door on the ribbon holds the theme, the colour-vision mode and, after #2958, the viewport line width and the anti-aliasing. Line width and anti-aliasing are not part of a theme. A user does not look for them in a menu named "Theme".
- The browser pane holds "Show origin names" (#645).
- The **Panels** (View) door holds the panel layout and the saved panel setups (#2339).
- The GPU choice is a command-line option (`--gpu`, #74).
- Other per-user choices are on the pages that use them: "Import tool holders" (#889) on the Tool library page, "Offline only" (#1945) in the AI Chat.

Each new display option must find a menu. The Theme list becomes long: after #2958 it has 18 rows.

## Proposal

Add one **Settings** window for the per-user application settings. It opens from the ribbon (a gear button at the right, near Donate), or from a menu entry. It has sections:

1. **Appearance**: theme, colour vision.
2. **Viewport / Graphics**:
   - Line width and anti-aliasing (#2958).
   - Show origin names.
   - Possible later items: the toolpath colours, the pick-highlight width, the ground grid.
3. **Graphics device** (read-only at first): the adapter and the backend that the app uses (`gpu_line`), and the sample counts that the device offers. Later, the preferred GPU (the setting behind `--gpu`).
4. **Tools and import**: "Import tool holders".
5. **AI**: "Offline only".

The Theme door can stay as a quick switch for the theme and the colour vision. Or it can open the Appearance section.

## Questions for the maintainer

1. Is the Settings window a dock panel (like Properties), or a separate window (like the tool shape window, #2397)?
2. Do the settings apply at once (as the theme picks do now), or with OK / Cancel?
3. Which settings move out of their current places, and which stay as shortcuts?
4. Does a per-user setting get an MCP tool or a CLI flag? The theme and colour vision have none today.

## Constraints

- The settings stay per-user (`prefs.json`, `view.json`). They are not in the project file and not on the undo history (#877).
- The UI rules apply: rows use the form helpers (#1122), and a page layout test is added (`layout_window_settings`).

## Done means

The maintainer answers the questions. The work is then split into sub-issues: the window, then one sub-issue for each section that moves.

Proposed labels: `enhancement`, `needs-research`, `P8`, `effort:high`, `area:ui`, `source:agent`

title: Viewport: the thick pick-outline highlight becomes a wedge that grows to the viewport edge at a low view angle

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:ui
labels.description: User interface and picking

labels.name: effort:medium
labels.description: One module or crate, a known pattern (issue-worker-medium)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body: ## What happens When an operation's Geometry has a picked face, the viewport draws the face outline as a thick violet stroke with a dark halo (`pick_ink` -> `pick_highlight_mesh::paint_selected`, #1505). Seen from a low angle, the stroke becomes a wedge: a second violet line separates from the outline and grows wider toward the edge of the viewport, until it reaches the edge. - The wedge shows in all themes (dark and light). - The line width and the anti-aliasing do not change it. It shows at 1 pt with anti-aliasing Off on the #2958 branch. ## Where it comes from These three builds were compared at the same low view of the same project (a picked top face, Face operation): | Build | Result | |---|---| | v0.24.0 release | No wedge. Some halo segments disappear at some angles and zoom levels (see below). | | `main` at acd5b02d3 | Wedge | | `main` + #2989 | Wedge | The pick highlight was rewritten after v0.24.0, in PR #2256 (#2201: cached geometry, one batched mesh of stroke paths). Thus the wedge is a regression of that change. - A probe of `egui::epaint::Tessellator` with a thin, acute closed path does not extend past its points. Thus a miter at a sharp corner is probably not the cause. - A likely cause is the screen projection of the world points. `push_screen_polyline_runs` projects each point by itself (`interact::project_uv`). - A point behind the eye (`w <= 1e-6`) is dropped, and the run continues to the next point that projects. - A point just in front of the near plane projects to a very large screen position. - Neither case clips the segment at the near plane, so a run can connect two points that are not neighbours on the outline, or go to a point far off the screen. ## Related: the halo that disappears (also in v0.24.0) In v0.24.0, at some angles and zoom levels, parts of the thick stroke disappear, and only the thin depth-tested overlay line stays. The cause is the same projection: a segment with an end behind the eye is dropped. This is older than the wedge. ## Expected The thick pick outline follows the picked edges at each angle and zoom. A segment that crosses the near plane is clipped at the near plane. It is not dropped, and it is not connected to another part of the outline. ## Done means - Each segment of the selected-pick and hover highlights is clipped at the near plane in clip space before it is projected. - A run never joins two points that are not neighbours on the outline. - A test with a picked rectangle seen from a low angle, with a corner behind the eye: - Each stroke vertex stays within the stroke width of the projected (clipped) outline. - No segment of the outline is missing. Found during the test of #2958 (PR #2989). #2989 does not change this code. Proposed labels: `bug`, `P3`, `effort:medium`, `area:ui`, `source:agent`

body:
Found by the release QA swarm (#2582) on **v0.24.0** with SolidCraft 0.45.0, driven through MCP by a Codex agent. Part: turned pin, Ø30 head / Ø24 body / M16x1.5 x 17 external thread with relief, 70 long, Tormach 15L Slant-PRO, Tormach PathPilot Lathe post.

## What happens
Threading says it cuts a modelled thread (`threading cuts a MODELED thread (a revolved V section); a smooth bar has none to find`). A real modelled thread from SolidCraft (`solid.thread`, `designation:"M16x1.5"`, `modeled:true`) cannot be threaded either way it is brought in:

1. **STEP** (`q03-turn-shaft-modeled.step`, imports 14388 facets with no reduced-fidelity warning):
   `M16Modeled: the source model cannot be sliced: the mesh is open at z = 16.687498017218555: 4 dangling chord ends`
   An STL exported from the same body is watertight (checked at 1e-6..1e-4 mm), so the open chain looks like CamCraft's tessellation/slicing of the helical faces.
2. **Native .sc** (`q03-turn-shaft.sc`, 29022 facets):
   `M16Native: invalid machining parameters: every axis fits this model equally - it curves the same the world around; domed ground is 5-Axis Contour or Parallel work`
   The part is a 30 x 30 x 70 turned shaft on Z; compare #152 (same message, cross hole).

On the smooth-envelope model the thread op generates, but verify then holds the post as `finish envelope near move 198: 0.9201 mm gouge, 8.0000 mm rest` (correctly - the model has no thread). So there is no route to a posted single-point thread from a SolidCraft part.

## Expected
A turned part with a modelled helical thread finds the Z axis and threads; or the refusal says plainly that helical models are not read yet and what to model instead.

## Reproduce (on skull)
- `/home/mikekinney/qa/runs/20261120-q03-turn-shaft/modeled-step-slice-failure.camproj` -> `open_project`, `generate {name:"M16Modeled"}`
- `/home/mikekinney/qa/runs/20261120-q03-turn-shaft/modeled-native-thread-test.camproj` -> `open_project`, `generate {name:"M16Native"}`
- smooth model: `/home/mikekinney/qa/runs/20261120-q03-turn-shaft/q03-turn-shaft.camproj` -> `verify {}`
Report: `/home/mikekinney/qa/runs/20261120-q03-turn-shaft/REPORT.md` (problems 2-4), calls in `/home/mikekinney/qa/runs/20261120-q03-turn-shaft/STEPS.log`.

Related: #893 (no catalog insert fits M16x1.5: 0.866 too narrow, 1.732 too wide), #2879, #2880.

Not checked on current main.

Done means: the STEP and .sc versions of this part each either thread and post, or are refused with a message that names the helical thread as the reason; pinned by tests on a recorded mesh.

Found by the release QA swarm (#2582) on **v0.24.0**, driven through `camcraft-cli mcp` by a Codex agent. Part: plate with a Ø5.0 pilot 10 mm deep (for an M6 tap), Tormach 770MX.

A spot operation (cycle `spot`) with a **Ø6, 120° point** drill, 1 mm deep (entry_z 12, floor_z 11) on 5 hole centres is refused:

```

post: post blocked - 1 warning(s): Spot5: move 11 cuts past the finish surface
```
At 1 mm point depth a 120° tip cuts a radius of tan(60°) x 1 = 1.73 mm, inside the 2.5 mm radius of the Ø5 bore, so nothing past the finish surface is cut. The stock sim reports 0 gouge. Changing only the tool diameter to 4 makes the same op verify and post. It looks like the check sweeps the nominal Ø6 cylinder, not the cone that actually enters (compare #266 for taps).

## Expected
A shallow spot whose cone stays inside the hole is not a gouge.

title: Compact pattern posting: opt-in G52 local coordinate shift and M98/M99 subprograms for verified posts

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:post
labels.description: Post processors and G-code

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P6
labels.description: Accepted enhancement, not scheduled

body:
## Goal

Add an opt-in compact post output mode for linear and grid pattern folders that uses local coordinate shifts (`G52`) and subprograms (`M98`/`M99` or dialect equivalent) on verified posts to reduce program size for high-count plate jobs. Depends on the pattern folder sub-issue of `#2938`.

## Scope

- **Output mode (`crates/app/src/schema.rs`, commands, MCP, project file):** Add an optional `PatternPostMode` setting on `PatternDef` with `Expanded` (default), `LocalShift` (`G52`), and `Subprogram` (`G52` + subprogram calls). Keep `Expanded` as the default so existing goldens do not change.
- **Post manifest capabilities (`assets/posts/AGENTS.md`, `crates/post/src/`):**
  - Add explicit opt-in manifest flags (`localShift = true`, `subprograms = true`) and CNC intermediate records or hooks for local shifts and subprogram calls.
  - Refuse by name any post script that does not declare the requested capability (matching `wcsRotation` and `axisInversion` refusal laws).
  - Refuse `LocalShift` or `Subprogram` for mirror folders and rotary circular patterns (a `G52` shift translates only and cannot mirror or index a rotary axis).
- **Verified dialects (`assets/posts/*.cps`):**
  - Implement and cite public control manuals (RS-274 / ISO 6983, Fanuc, Haas, LinuxCNC) for the first verified set: `fanuc.cps`, `haas.cps`, `doosan-dnm.cps`, `mazak.cps`, `mach4.cps` (`G52` + `M98`/`M99`), and `tormach.cps` (`G52` + LinuxCNC `O<sub> call`).
  - Always cancel local shift (`G52 X0. Y0. Z0.`) before every tool change, after the pattern, and at program end.

## Done means

Golden NC tests and a coordinate-interpreter verification test prove that `LocalShift` and `Subprogram` output cuts the exact same world coordinates as `Expanded` moves, cancels `G52 X0. Y0. Z0.` before tool changes and program end, and refuses undeclared posts and mirror/rotary folders by name.

## Goal

  - Transform each enabled copy `k` using `cl::transform::transform_xy` at `k * angle_step_deg` around `center`.
  - Run full stock simulation, stock bounds, fixture collision, and machine travel checks on all enabled copies.

## Done means

Tests post an indexed 4-sided A-axis circular pattern on a 4-axis machine with safe retract before each index, refuse indexing by name when rotary travel or `index_swing` clearance fails, and post and simulate a planar XY circular pattern on a 3-axis mill.

body:
## Goal

Add vertical-plane mirror support to pattern folders so users can program one half of a symmetrical part and mirror its toolpaths to the other half with full model verification. Depends on the CL toolpath transforms, pattern folder, and pattern verification sub-issues of `#2938`.

## Scope

- **Mirror mode (`crates/app/src/schema.rs`, commands, MCP, project file):** Add `Mirror { plane_point, plane_normal, cut_direction, keep_original }` to `PatternDef`.
  - Allow vertical planes only (`nz == 0`); refuse horizontal or tilted mirror planes at command creation.
  - Add `MirrorCutDirection` with `PreserveClimb` (default) and `GeometricMirror`.
  - Support `keep_original` (default `true`, matching copies `0` and `1`; copy `0` can also be disabled via `disabled_instances`).
- **Transform and posting (`crates/cl/src/cl/transform.rs`, `crates/app/src/posting.rs`):**
  - Under `GeometricMirror`, reflect moves, flip `arc.ccw` (`G2` <-> `G3`), and swap `CompSide` (`G41` <-> `G42`).
  - Under `PreserveClimb`, use safe per-pass reversal for 2D contours, profiles, and chamfers, and refuse by name any operation with ramps, adaptive clearing, or multi-pass roughing that cannot reverse safely.
  - Refuse unsupported operation kinds (turning, threading, probing, wire EDM, sinker EDM, tilted 5-axis moves) by name.
- **Full model verification (`crates/app/src/posting.rs`, `crates/app/src/stock_sim.rs`):**
  - Carve the mirrored copy into the stock simulation and judge it against the full part mesh (`deviate`).
  - Run live model gouge, shank, and rapid-in-stock verification (`crates/sim/src/verify/`, `crates/app/src/operation/kept_rejudge.rs`) and fixture checks on every mirrored toolpath so sub-lattice gouges and shank hits on the mirrored side block the post.

## Done means

## Scope

- **Translation (`translate`):** Shift every move, arc center, `Cycle`, `CompSpan`, `EdgeBreak`, and `PlasmaCut` by `(dx, dy, dz)`. Keep coordinates finite and snapped consistently with `crates/cl/src/cl/moves.rs` (`lattice`).

Refuse by name any path whose entry or engagement cannot reverse safely (helical ramps, adaptive clearing, multi-pass roughing).

Unit tests in `crates/cl/` verify micron-accurate translation, XY rotation, A/B axis rotation, vertical-plane mirroring (`G2`/`G3` and `G41`/`G42` swap), safe 2D contour pass reversal under `PreserveClimb`, and named refusals for unsupported records and horizontal mirror planes.

## What happens

Indexed pocket operations can report a false shank collision with stock.
Found while building the catalog case for #2868, part of #2392.

The original blank spans X/Y -30..30 and Z0..70 mm.
The two side pockets use A+90/B0 and A-90/B0.

The 6 mm EM-0600-4FL cutter has a 15 mm flute length and no holder.
Generation reports shank collisions with uncut stock. Verification holds both operations.

## Cause

At upstream/main 58cb641ca, operation/generate.rs:205-206 computes stock_top_z in world coordinates.
At line 3638, the tilted branch initializes st_local with this world value minus origin Z.
Lines 3659-3666 only increase this value with projected box corners.
The correct local cap of 30 cannot replace the initial world value of 70.
The local shank bottom is about 41 mm at the pocket floor.
It clears the real stock cap of 30, but not the incorrect cap of 70.
The local verification therefore reports a collision.
stock_top_law.rs only rechecks RapidInStock warnings against the exact solids.
It does not recheck ShankHit warnings.

This differs from closed #903, which concerns the tilted band exclusion region.
The conservative box cap for an oblique face is a separate limitation.

Compute the stock cap in the coordinate frame of the path under test.
Do not retain a world height as a lower bound for a local height.
Keep true shank collisions blocked.

## Done means

A pin with world Z70 and A+90/B0 uses the projected local stock cap of 30.
The A-90/B0 case has the same result.
A safe shank above the real stock cap passes. A real collision still blocks posting.

- A program whose line count follows from its toolpath posts; the guard scales with the input (e.g. a bound derived from the number of moves/operations), or is far higher than any real toolpath, and still stops a runaway script.
- If a limit still refuses, the refusal names the limit, the line count reached and the operation.

The maintainer decided on 2026-11-20: widen the verdict tolerance for a model that opens at reduced accuracy. This issue holds that work. Part of #2976.

## What happens

PR #2994 (issue #2976) opens a STEP file whose edges lie as far off their surfaces as the tolerance that the file states. The model is meshed at a coarser tolerance (up to 0.02 mm) and gets the reduced-fidelity flag and a note.

A program on that model cannot be posted. The fidelity law (#864) permits a verdict only while the excess of the mesh tolerance over the import chord is inside `DEV_TOL` (0.01 mm). The measured case: the chord is 0.02 mm, the import chord is 0.005 mm, so the excess is 0.015 mm. The law then has no verdict tolerance, and each operation is refused by name unless its stock to leave covers the excess. A finishing operation thus cannot post. The command `VouchModelFidelity` does not apply, because the chord is a measured value.

The file is legal and it opens. The user has a workaround only for roughing (stock to leave). Thus the priority is `P3`.

## What is wanted

- The verdict tolerance of such a model is the mesh deviation of the model itself, with a hard upper limit (for example 0.02 mm). The limit is a constant that no file can raise.
- The posted program says so: a comment in the program header names the model and the tolerance that the checks used. The UI shows the same fact as a note in plain English.
- The vouch command is not the mechanism for this.

## Safety

The gouge check must stay conservative in the direction that matters: the tool must not cut deeper than the real surface permits.

- The mesh can stand inside or outside the real surface by its deviation. The check must not count that deviation in favour of the tool. State the rule for each direction (a cut into the part, and material left on the part), and why a gouge of the real surface larger than the limit still blocks the post.
- The stock simulation, the keep law, the rest material and the collision checks each read the verdict tolerance. List each reader and what changes in it.
- A model at full fidelity keeps today's law, with no change of any verdict.

## Done when

- A test with a model at reduced accuracy (our own fixture, mesh deviation just under the limit) pins that a finishing operation posts, and that the program header has the note.
- A test just over the limit pins the refusal by name.
- A test pins that a real gouge deeper than the verdict tolerance still blocks the post on such a model.
- Each full-fidelity pin of the fidelity law stays green and unchanged.
- The decision file names the rule, the limit and what the user loses.

## Order

The code needs PR #2994 on `main`. The research does not.

Part of #2976. Refs #2994, #864

body:
Found by the read-only review of PR #2985 (issue #2901). The PR records the gap in its decision file. This issue tracks it.

## What happens

PR #2985 adds the law `first_traverse_low`: the clearance plane of a milling operation must be above the top of the start stock and of each fixture, because the first traverse starts from an X/Y that is not known.

In a 3+2 frame the law does not read the box of the machine table (`crates/app/src/operation/first_traverse.rs:89-99`). The table box is a slab about 1,000,000 mm wide. Read along a tilted tool axis, its "top" is very large, and each indexed operation was refused. The PR thus skips the table when the frame is tilted. An upright frame still reads the table. The stock and the fixtures are read in each frame.

What stays without a check: the first traverse of each 3+2 operation against the machine table. A tilted clearance plane goes down toward the table on its low side, about 0.36 mm for each mm of travel at B 20 degrees. A real table can thus stand above the plane inside the travel of the machine. That is a collision that passes. Thus the priority is `P1`.

## Possible repair

Clip the table box to the travel of the machine (the machine file has the axis limits) before the corner reading. Then the law can read the table in a tilted frame.

## Done when

- A 3+2 operation whose clearance plane goes under the table top inside the machine travel is refused by name.
- The indexed example operations that post today still post.
- A machine file with no axis limits gives a defined result (a refusal or a note), not a silent pass.

Refs #2901, #2965

title: STEP model import: the short name of PLANE_ANGLE_UNIT is not read, so an angle in degrees can be read as radians

labels.name: bug

body:
Found by the read-only second review of PR #2927. The finding comes from a read of the code. No run proves it.

## What can happen

A STEP file can use the short entity names of ISO 10303-21. The short name of `PLANE_ANGLE_UNIT` is `PLANUN` (public ISO short-name registry, `https://standards.iso.org/iso/10303/tech/short_names/short-names.txt`, line 1554). The solidcore p21 parser does not map this name, and PR #2927 does not add it.

A file that states its angle unit as degrees with the short name then has no angle unit that the reader can find. The reader uses radians. An angle that the file gives in degrees, for example the semi-angle of a cone, is then read as radians. The surface has the wrong shape, and no refusal or note tells the user.

Wrong geometry is wrong output for each toolpath and each gouge check. Thus the priority is `P1` until a test shows the correct angle or a refusal.

## Where

- `crates/kernel/src/solidcore_step.rs`: the rename step that PR #2927 adds for `GUAC` and `SUNT`, and the unit read after it.
- The same registry gives `GC` for `GLOBAL_UNCERTAINTY_ASSIGNED_CONTEXT`. It is not mapped. That changes the tolerance only: check it in the same work.

## What is expected

- The reader reads the angle unit of a short-name file, or
- a file that has an angle unit that the reader cannot resolve is refused by name. An angle is never read in a unit that the file does not state.

## Done when

- A STEP fixture that we made, with short names and a cone whose angle is in degrees, is in `testdata/models/`.
- A test imports it. The cone has the correct angle (checked by a size that depends on the angle), or the import is refused by name.

title: Viewport: draw toolpaths and height planes as wide anti-aliased lines, with MSAA and a depth offset

labels.name: enhancement

body: ## Problem The viewport draws toolpaths, height-plane rectangles, region outlines and the other overlay lines as `wgpu` `LineList` primitives (`crates/ui/src/viewport.rs`, `overlay_pipeline`). A `wgpu` line is always 1 hardware pixel wide. The viewport targets use `sample_count: 1`, thus the lines also have no anti-aliasing. The result: - The lines are thin and jagged. On a display with 150 % scale, they are thinner again. - The feed colour (green) has low contrast against the grey stock. It is hard to see the paths and the direction chevrons. - The WCS triad does not have this problem. egui draws it again over the GPU image with a 3 px anti-aliased stroke (#195, `GIZMO_STROKE_PX`). Thus the triad is much easier to see than the toolpath. ## Trial A trial on a local branch (not pushed) rendered `examples/first-part.camproj` through the real viewport pipelines (`gpu_render` test harness). The operation Face1 is open, thus its height planes show. **1. Close view. Before: today. After: 1.5 px wide lines, MSAA 4x, depth offset.** **2. Full view. 1.5 px stays clear when the camera is far. 2 px and 2.5 px made the dense paths into one solid area, thus 1.5 px is the default.** **3. Depth offset. Without it, a wide line that lies on a face is half hidden by the depth test. The line then shows thin and broken. With the offset, the line has its full width.** ## Proposed change 1. **Wide lines.** Draw each overlay segment as a quad that faces the screen (two triangles). The vertex shader extends the quad to the line width in pixels. The fragment shader fades the edges for anti-aliasing. - Use one instance for each segment (36 bytes), and make the 6 corners in the shader. Do not write 6 full vertices for each segment. At the overlay limit (`MAX_OVERLAY_VERTICES`, 512k segments), the trial layout used approximately 135 MB. The instanced layout uses approximately 18 MB, which is less than the current 24 MB. - Extend each end by half the line width and fade the end. Then two lines that meet at a corner (for example, a height-plane rectangle) close the corner and do not overlap past it. 2. **Line width setting.** The default is 1.5 pt. The range is approximately 1 to 3 pt. Multiply the value by the pixels-per-point of the display. 3. **Depth offset.** Move each wide-line vertex toward the eye by approximately 3 line widths of world distance. Calculate the world size of one pixel from the `mvp` matrix (the length of its y row), thus the offset is correct in perspective and in orthographic projection. In perspective, the vertex moves along the eye ray, thus the line does not move on the screen. - Effect: a line that is behind a face by less than approximately 3 line widths shows through. This is a few pixels of depth on the screen, which is much less than a real feature. 4. **MSAA setting: Off, 2x, 4x.** The default is 4x. - All viewport pipelines and the trace composite pipeline (`crates/ui/src/trace/composite.rs`) must use the same sample count. The pass renders into a multisampled target and resolves into the current colour texture. - WebGPU guarantees only 1 and 4 samples. 2x needs the device feature `TEXTURE_ADAPTER_SPECIFIC_FORMAT_FEATURES` and a check of the adapter's sample counts for the colour and depth formats. If the adapter does not support a count, do not show it, or use the nearest supported count and write a log line. - The web build shows Off and 4x only. ## Cost - **MSAA 4x memory.** The colour and depth targets have 4 samples. At 2560×1440, this is approximately 120 MB more GPU memory. At 4K, it is approximately 265 MB. 2x uses half. An integrated GPU is the most sensitive, thus MSAA is a setting. - **MSAA and the traced stock.** The composite writes `frag_depth` once for each pixel. Thus MSAA does not smooth the traced stock edges. Its cost does not change. - **Wide lines.** The overlay uploads only when the scene digest changes (`view_pass::sync_scene`), not when the camera moves. The GPU does approximately 3 times more vertex work and blends approximately 3 to 4 times more line pixels. This is small compared to the model mesh. - Measure the frame time before and after with the `frame_cost` timers, on a large toolpath and on an integrated GPU. Write the readings in the PR. ## Not changed - The geometry, the toolpaths and the posted G-code do not change. This is a display change only. - The pixel goldens (`docs/images/`, `crates/ui/tests/snapshots/`) change at the cut, not in the PR (AGENTS.md "Pixel snapshots are release-lane"). ## Done means - Toolpaths, height planes, region outlines and the other overlay lines draw as anti-aliased lines of the set width. The default is 1.5 pt, multiplied by the pixels-per-point of the display. - A line that lies on a face shows its full width. - The corners of a height-plane rectangle close and do not overlap past the corner. - The MSAA setting (Off / 2x / 4x) and the line width setting persist. An unsupported sample count does not crash and writes a log line. - Tests: - A GPU readback test shows that a line on a face has its full width. - A test shows the instanced buffer size for each segment. - A test shows the fallback of an unsupported sample count. - The PR has the frame-time readings. Proposed labels: `enhancement`, `P6`, `effort:medium`, `area:ui`, `source:agent`

PR #2940 exempts a loop from the partly-bevelled refusal of #2887 when the top section is the wall section moved rigidly (`leans` in `crates/motion/src/machining2d/chamfer_ride.rs`). That is correct for a wall that leans in a tilted frame.

title: Toolpath patterns and mirrors: replicate operations in a linear, grid or circular (rotary) pattern, or mirror them across a plane

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:sim
labels.description: Stock simulation and verification

labels.name: area:post
labels.description: Post processors and G-code

labels.name: needs-research
labels.description: Large idea with open questions: research and file sub-issues before any code

labels.name: effort:max
labels.description: New algorithms, formats or open design (issue-worker-max)

labels.name: P8
labels.description: Larger idea needing design or research before code

body:
Requested by @vilts.

## Goal

Replicate toolpaths that are already calculated, so that the user does not program the same feature many times. There are two methods:

1. **Pattern.** Copy the toolpaths to more positions:
   - **Linear pattern:** copies in one direction (count and spacing).
   - **Grid pattern:** copies in two directions (count and spacing in each direction).
   - **Circular pattern:** copies around a rotary axis (count and angle step). The machine indexes the rotary axis to each copy.
2. **Mirror.** Copy the toolpaths to the other side of a plane that the user selects.

## Proposed structure

- A new **pattern folder** inside a setup. It holds one or more operations of that setup.
- The user sets the pattern or the mirror on the folder. The folder replicates each operation in it.
- A change to an operation in the folder changes all its copies.

## Use cases

- **Plate work:** put one model in a corner of the plate, program it, then replicate it 100 times over the plate.
- **Symmetrical part:** program one half of the part, then mirror the toolpaths to the other half.

## Checks

- **Pattern:** the operations in the folder are checked against the original model. The copies are replicated over the stock. They do not have a model of their own to check against.
- **Mirror:** the mirror is on the same part, so each mirrored toolpath gets the full checks against the model (gouges and the other checks).

## Open questions for research

The requester's suggestions for questions 1-5 are a start point. They are not decisions. The research can change them, and it records the reason for each change.

1. **Folder:** is the folder an operation group in the setup tree? Can a folder hold another folder? Can the user turn off one copy (for example, a position with a clamp)?
   - *Suggestion:* a folder inside the setup, not a separate setup with a different WCS for each copy. All copies use the WCS of the setup. The user can turn off one copy.
2. **Order of the copies:** does the post cut all operations at one copy, then go to the next copy? Or does it cut one operation at each copy, then go to the next operation (fewer tool changes)? Is this a folder setting?
   - *Suggestion:* a folder setting with two values:
     - **By part:** finish one copy completely, then go to the next copy.
     - **By tool:** cut with one tool at each copy, then change to the next tool.
3. **Posted output:** does the post write each copy as expanded moves? Or does it use subprograms (`M98`, `G65`), local coordinate shifts (`G52`) or more work offsets (`G54.1 P..`)? Which of these does each built-in post support?
   - *Suggestion:*
     - Default: one full program with the moves of each copy written out.
     - Option: subprograms.
     - Option: a coordinate shift (`G52`), which makes the program smaller.
     - No work offset for each copy: the number of work offsets limits the number of copies, and a work offset cannot mirror.
4. **Circular pattern:** the request is a pattern around a rotary axis (indexed A or B). Is a circular pattern in the XY plane, around a point, also necessary on a 3-axis machine?
   - *Suggestion:* not necessary on a 3-axis machine.
5. **Mirror and cut direction:** a mirror changes climb milling into conventional milling. It also swaps `G2`/`G3` and the compensation side (`G41`/`G42`). Does the mirror keep the climb direction of the original (the path is reversed), or is this a setting?
   - *Suggestion:* a setting. The default keeps the cut direction that the user set on the operation: a climb cut stays a climb cut.
6. **Checks of the copies:** what is the minimum check for a pattern copy? For example: the copy stays inside the stock, the copy does not hit a fixture or a clamp, and the stock simulation includes all copies. A copy that fails a check must block the post (AGENTS.md "Never Crash, Never Gouge").
7. **Commands:** the folder, the pattern and the mirror need undoable commands and MCP tools (AGENTS.md "Everything Is a Command").
8. **Relation to nesting:** #2166 copies a part's operations to each nested position on a router sheet. Can the two features use the same transform of a toolpath?

## Related

- #2166 Nesting: copies the operations of a part to each placed position.
- #1720 WCS flip.

## Done means

The open questions above have answers in the comments of this issue. The sub-issues for the work are filed with their priorities and effort labels and linked here. Then this issue closes.

Proposed labels (I cannot set labels): `enhancement`, `needs-research`, `P?`, `effort:max`, `area:post`, `area:multiaxis`, `area:sim`, `area:ui`, `source:agent`.

body:
Found by the read-only review of PR #2918 (comment of 2026-11-20). The finding comes from a read of the code. No run proves it yet.

## What can happen

A STEP file can use the short entity names of ISO 10303-21. The solidcore p21 parser changes some short names to the long names (`SHORT_NAMES`, `solidcore-record/src/step/p21.rs:614-659` at the pinned revision), for example `A2PL3D`, `CRTPNT`, `DRCTN` and `LNGUNT`. It does not change the short forms of `GLOBAL_UNIT_ASSIGNED_CONTEXT` and `SI_UNIT`.

The unit read of the model import (`length_units` in `camcraft-kernel`, and the units module of solidcore) finds only the long name `GLOBAL_UNIT_ASSIGNED_CONTEXT`. Thus a short-name file gives geometry but no unit context. If the reader then uses 1 mm for each unit, a model in inches or metres has the wrong size by a factor of 25.4 or 1000. No refusal or note tells the user.

Wrong geometry is wrong output for each toolpath and each gouge check. Thus the priority is `P1` until a test shows a refusal.

## Where

- `crates/kernel/src/solidcore_step.rs` (`length_units`, near line 244).
- The same defect class in the tool-body read is a blocker of PR #2918 (`crates/geometry/src/step_csys_read.rs:28-30`, `crates/geometry/src/step_units.rs:37-62`). That PR repairs the tool-body read only.

## Not known

- If the reader before PR #2904 (truck-stepio) had the same result for short-name files.
- If a CAD system that our users have writes short names. The form is legal but not common.

## What is expected

- A file that has geometry and a length-unit record, but no unit context that the reader can find, is refused by name. The unit laws of #306 and #689 apply.
- Better: the reader knows the short names of the unit entities and reads the unit.

## Done when

- A STEP fixture that we made, with short entity names and an inch unit, is in `testdata/models/`.
- A test imports it. The result is the correct size in millimetres, or a refusal that names the missing unit context. The result is never a model at 1 mm for each unit.
- The same test set has a metre file.

Refs #917

body:
This issue holds the part of #1868 that its pull request does not do. Part of #1452.

## What works after #1868

A `Slot` or a `Trochoidal Slot` reads one picked chain of a DXF profile:

- one closed line-arc slot outline (it seeds `a`, `b` and `width`);
- one open straight chain as the centerline (it seeds `a` and `b`).

## What is refused by name today

1. An open chain that is not straight (an arc, or a chain of lines and arcs). The message is "the picked centerline is not straight".
2. A closed chain used as a centerline (a circular groove). A closed chain is read as a slot outline only.
3. A selection with more than one chain (a layer of slots). The message is "a slot on a DXF profile cuts one chain".

## Why it is not in #1868

- `OpParams::Slot` and `OpParams::TrochoidalSlot` hold two points and one width. The generator, the machine area (`material_source.rs`), the fit law (`slot_fit.rs`, `slot_room.rs`) and the WCS rotation read these numbers.
- A curved channel needs a new parameter form. That is a project file change with a version bump.
- The plain Slot generator (`machining2d::slot`) cuts a straight channel only. A curved channel with a width larger than the tool needs offset rows along a chain. That is a new algorithm.
- `machining2d::trochoidal_slot` takes a point chain already. Its machine area and its fit law do not.

## Scope

- Let the two slot kinds follow a curved centerline at the typed width.
- Make the machine area the sweep of the centerline. The verification and the stock simulation must use it.
- Decide how a closed chain is read: as an outline or as a centerline. A wrong guess cuts in the wrong place, so the user must choose.
- Let one operation cut each chain of a selection, or keep one chain for each operation and say so in the user guide.

## Done means

- A `Slot` and a `Trochoidal Slot` on an open line-arc chain generate passes that stay inside the swept channel. A golden CL file pins each.
- A channel narrower than the tool, and a centerline with a corner tighter than the tool can follow, are refused by name.
- The straight slots of #1868 and the two-point `.camproj` slots give the same output as before.

## Evidence

- `crates/app/src/operation/slot_sketch.rs` (`resolve`) and `crates/motion/src/machining2d/slot_room_line.rs` (`from_centerline`) hold the refusals.
- `crates/app/tests/slot_dxf_sketch.rs`, test `picks_that_are_no_slot_are_refused_by_name`, pins them.
- `docs/decisions/1868-slot-dxf-sketches.md` records the decision.

Priority note: this is a follow-up that an agent found during work, so it has `P7` by the rule. It is the remaining scope of a `P4` issue. The maintainer can raise it.

body:
The maintainer asked for this on 2026-11-20, after he saw that only one of the three runners works:

> The issue would need to not only split the post work into several "lanes" - it would also need to produce artifacts that gets collected and handed back for inspection. All the lanes could then be queued if we reduce the amount of runner but also run in parallell when we have more runners..

Now: `post-merge.yml` has one job, `gate`. It runs the whole batch tier (about 950 steps) on one runner. The runners `wopr` and `uma` have the label `camcraft-post-merge`. One of them works and the other waits. A run lasts about 40 minutes. The concurrency group `post-merge-main` allows one run at a time. A new push queues behind the running gate or cancels it.

Wanted:
- The batch tier is split into lanes. Each lane is one job of the workflow, for example a matrix over groups of test binaries, clippy, and the build.
- The lanes are independent. With three runners, three lanes run at the same time. With one runner, the lanes queue and give the same result as today.
- Each lane writes its logs and its result to an artifact (`gate-logs/` as `xtask gate` makes them). A final job collects all artifacts. It writes one verdict, with the red steps named, for the rolling issue `main is red (post-merge gate)`.
- A person or an agent can download the artifact of any lane and read the failure without a second run. The verdict names each lane, its runner, its time and its result.
- The report job (known defect #1611: skipped) is repaired or replaced as part of this work.

Open questions for the work:
- How `cargo xtask gate batch` splits into lanes: by a flag such as `--lane N/M`, or by named groups. The split must be deterministic, and each test binary must run in exactly one lane.
- How lanes share the build. Each runner builds the debug test binaries one time, or one job builds and uploads them. The compile cache (`sccache`) and the size of the artifacts matter here.
- How the lanes treat a push during a run (cancel all lanes, or finish and queue).
- Whether `m3` (macOS, label `camcraft-pr-test`) can join. The label rule in the `runners` skill allows a trigger only on `main` and only for self-hosted runners.

Safety (AGENTS.md "GitHub Actions minutes are budgeted"):
- No new `push`, `pull_request` or `schedule` trigger. The triggers stay as they are.
- No lane runs code of a fork PR on a self-hosted runner.
- The change touches process files (`xtask/`, the workflow, the `gate` and `runners` skills). The PR body has the line `Process change: yes`. The merging session bumps `PROCESS_VERSION` after the merge.

Done means: one push to `main` runs at least two lanes at the same time when two runners are free. The lanes together run the same test binaries as the batch tier today, with no binary lost. The collector job gives one verdict with the artifacts attached. The `runners` and `gate` skills describe the lanes.

Related: #1611 (report job skipped).

body:
## What

A Slot with a width larger than the tool diameter leaves material in its two round ends. `verify` reports no problem, and the post is not blocked.

The work on the example case `2d/slots` (#2861, part of #2392) found this.

## How to reproduce

On `main` at `ab9955105`, run this script with a model `slots` (a 100 x 60 x 12 mm block, stock of the same size):

```js
cam.call("add_tool", { catalog: "EM-0600-4FL", holder: "none" });
cam.call("add_operation", {
  kind: "Slot", name: "Slot1", tool: "EM-0600-4FL", source: "slots",
  params: {
    a: [-25.0, 15.0], b: [25.0, 15.0], width: 10.0, stock_to_leave: 0.0,
    top_z: { reference: "top_of_stock", offset: 0.0 },
    bottom_z: { reference: "top_of_stock", offset: -6.0 },
    stepdown: 3.0, stepover: 2.0, feed: 600.0, plunge_feed: 150.0, climb: true
  }
});
cam.generate();
cam.verify();   // ok
```

## What the program does

The tool is 6 mm and the slot is 10 mm wide. The tool centre must stay in a stadium of 2 mm radius around the line `a -> b`. Each level posts three rows:

```
G01 X-25. Y13. Z9. F150
G01 X25. Y13. Z9. F600
G01 X27. Y15. Z9. F600
G01 X-27. Y15. Z9. F600
G01 X-25. Y17. Z9. F600
G01 X25. Y17. Z9. F600
```

The rows touch the round end only at their end points. The tool does not follow the arc between two row ends. The move between two rows is a straight line (a chord), not an arc.

## Measured

A point check of the 10 mm stadium against the tool centre path gives these results:

- The largest leftover is 0.86 mm, on the wall of each round end at 45 degrees, where no move joins two rows.
- The leftover is 0.59 mm at the two corners where a chord joins two rows.
- The total area that is not cut is about 8.9 mm2 for each level.

The straight walls are correct. The rows at `Y13` and `Y17` cut them to size.

## Expected

One of these:

- The Slot cuts its full outline. For example, the tool follows the two half circles of the tool centre stadium at each level.
- The operation reports the leftover as a warning that names the Slot and the largest leftover.

## Workaround

- Use a smaller `stepover`. The leftover becomes smaller, but it does not go to zero.
- Use a Trochoidal slot of the same width. Its last move is a half circle around `b`, and its entry is a full circle around `a`.

## Notes

- The row law is in `crates/motion/src/machining2d/slots.rs` (`SlotParams`: "each row reaches the round ends exactly as far as it can").
- The case `examples/catalog/2d/slots` shows the two programs side by side. A fix changes `slots.nc` of that case. Run `cargo xtask catalog --case 2d/slots` with the fix.

## What happens

Each 2D and 3D milling path starts with a rapid from (WCS X0 Y0, clearance) to the entry point of the operation. The machine never makes this move: after a tool change the X/Y position of the tool is not known.

- The viewport draws a rapid line from the WCS origin.
- The simulation moves the tool from the WCS origin. Between two operations it goes from the end of the first operation to the WCS origin, then to the entry of the next one.
- The fixture checks and the link router judge this move. If the line from the WCS origin to the entry strikes a fixture, `plan_links` lifts the link at the WCS origin. The post then writes `G00 Z<H>` and `G00 X0. Y0. Z<H>`: a real first move to the WCS origin. A fixture at the WCS corner can also give a false refusal or a false fixture hit.

## Where

- `crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs:3109-3117`: `path.seat_approach(Point3::new(0.0, 0.0, hl.clearance), [o.x, o.y])` puts the start at the WCS origin (#2382).
- `crates/cl/src/cl/path_approach.rs:30-49`: `Toolpath::seat_approach`.
- `crates/app/src/operation/fixture_route.rs:186-229`: `plan` lifts the link at the start X/Y.
- The seeds: `PathBuilder::approached(Point3::new(0.0, 0.0, p.clearance_z))` in `crates/motion/src/machining2d/*.rs` and `crates/motion/src/finishing3d/*.rs`.
- The tests that lock the current behaviour: `crates/app/tests/wcs_start.rs:143-170` (`opens_at`) and `crates/cl/tests/origin_approach.rs:62-99`.

## What is expected

- The WCS is only the reference of the coordinates. No move of the path starts or ends at the WCS origin unless the operation cuts there.
- The opening rapid starts over its own entry point, on the clearance plane: `from.x == to.x` and `from.y == to.y`. It stays a rapid (the approach law of #690 and #697).
- The posted program does not change when no fixture is struck. The current goldens stay byte-identical.
- With a fixture, the link router does not lift a link at the WCS origin. No `X0 Y0` block is posted for it.
- The 3+2 frame case and the yaw case keep their local frame (the call site reads the frame before the seat).

## Done when

- `seat_approach` seats the start over the end X/Y of the opening rapid, not over the WCS origin. Alternative: it is removed and the seeds do the same. Record the choice in `docs/decisions/`.
- `wcs_start.rs` asserts the new law for a face (2D), a 3D finish and a drill, with the WCS at the stock centre and at the stock corner. The opening rapid has no X/Y length, and no move starts at the WCS origin.
- A new pinning test in `crates/app/tests/` puts a fixture box between the WCS origin and the entry. The posted program has no `X0 Y0` block and no fixture refusal.

body:
The maintainer reported this in chat on 2026-11-20:

> Most machinists define their WCS at the center of a part or at a corner in a mill. This doesn't mean that the cutter starts from that WCS point, it just means that it references it. The fault would be that the cutter moves to the starting point as a first move. It doesn't have to. This is a general post-processing problem and operations calculation issue. The machine should move to its first starting point for an operation, in relation to the WCS, not start at the WCS. It doesn't matter where the WCS is. The first operation starts where it has to start to clear the part, but in relation to the WCS.

What the maintainer sees: the first move of an operation goes to the WCS origin (X0 Y0). It does not go to the start point that the operation needs.

Expected:
- The WCS is only the reference of the coordinates. It is not a point that the tool must visit.
- The first positioning move of each operation goes to the real start point of that operation: the entry position that clears the part and the stock.
- That point is written in coordinates of the WCS of the setup. It is correct for any WCS position (part center, corner, or elsewhere).

Why P1: a first move to a wrong point can move the tool into the part, the stock or the fixture at rapid. This is wrong output (Prime Directive).

Not known yet. The research answers these questions in comments:
- Where the defect shows: the toolpath in the viewport, the simulation, the CL file, the posted G-code, or several of these.
- If it is in the operation calculation (the first point of the toolpath), in the post (the initial move or the safe-start block), or in both.
- If it depends on the operation type, the entry type, the machine file, or the post dialect.
- If it is the same fault as the retired #2382 (coordinates measured from the world origin), or a different one. #2382 was about the origin of the coordinates. This issue is about the first move target.
- Which test or fixture proves it: a part with its WCS at the center and a part with its WCS at a corner, with the same operation.

Done means: a pinning test per operation family shows that the first move goes to the entry point of the operation in WCS coordinates, and not to X0 Y0, for a WCS at the center and at a corner. The research comment lists the files and the sub-issues.

Related: #2382 (closed).

- With no picks, ride only the modelled bevels, per segment rather than per whole loop, OR refuse at generation with a message that names the partly bevelled loop and asks for picks.
- Classify bevel vs sharp in a way that does not depend on tessellation (two-sided gap, or per segment).

body:
Found during the work on #2394 (example case turning/cone-thread).

## What happens

The Threading operation starts each pass at the top lattice point of the thread. This point is always inside the length of the part. A pass cannot start in front of the end face (see the related issue about the threading verdict).

With the post option "Threading: G76 cycle", the Fanuc lathe post writes one rapid to the start point and then the two G76 blocks. The start Z is the top lattice point.

A Fanuc-type control moves the insert from the start point to the depth of each pass at rapid traverse. It does this at the start Z. At that Z the bar is solid. Thus the control moves the threading insert into the material at rapid traverse, one time for each pass.

The G32 output of the same thread does not have this problem. It writes the infeed as a `G01` block at the plunge feed.

## Example

The case turning/cone-thread of #2394, with `set_post_options { "threading": "g76" }`, posts:

```
G00 X30.1 Z77.4
G76 P010000 Q250 R0.17
G76 X8.16 Z63.9 P920 Q250 F1.5
```

The part end face is at Z78. The thread diameter is 10 mm from Z63 to Z78. At Z77.4 the insert (1.2 mm wide) stands above solid material from Z76.8 to Z78.

The golden `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/fanuc-lathe/thread_g76.nc` has the same shape: `G00 X12.1 Z14.` on a bar that continues at 12 mm diameter to Z40.

## What is expected

A G76 cycle starts in free air: in front of the end face, or in a relief groove that is wider than the insert. If the start point is above material, the post refuses the G76 cycle by name. It does not write the cycle.

## Basis

The G76 motion (rapid infeed at the start Z, feed along Z, rapid retract, rapid return) is from the public Fanuc lathe programming manuals. No machine ran this program. A person with a Fanuc lathe or simulator must confirm the reading.

## Workaround

Use G32 passes (the default). The case of #2394 does this.

Refs #2394

body:
## What

`add_operation` refuses a 2D Contour whose `params` give a lead shape that is different from the seeded shape. The message does not name the cause.

Found during the work on #2859 (example case `2d/contour-tabs`). Part of #2392.

## Steps

Run this script with `camcraft-cli script` on `upstream/main` 5fdbed9bd. A stock, a model and the tool `EM-0600-4FL` are in the document.

```js
cam.call("add_operation", {
  kind: "2D Contour",
  tool: "EM-0600-4FL",
  source: "contour-tabs",
  params: { lead: { arc: { radius: 3.0 } } }
});
```

## Result

```
camcraft-cli: call: add_operation: bad params patch: invalid value: map, expected map with a single key
```

## Cause (as read from the behaviour)

The tool applies `params` as a JSON merge patch on the seeded parameters. The seeded lead is `{ "linear": { "length": 8.0 } }`. The merged value has the two keys `linear` and `arc`. The lead is an enum with one key, so the parse fails.

## Workaround

Remove the seeded key in the same patch:

```js
params: { lead: { linear: null, arc: { radius: 3.0 } } }
```

## Expected

One of these:

- The patch replaces the lead when it names a different shape.
- The refusal names the field and the cause, for example: `lead: give one shape only (found linear and arc)`.

The same merge applies to `edit_operation` and to each parameter that is an enum with data (`links.approach.lead_out` is one). The fix must cover them.

## Done means

A test in `crates/app/tests/` gives `lead: { arc: { radius: 3.0 } }` to `add_operation` and to `edit_operation` for a 2D Contour. The operation gets the arc lead, or the refusal names `lead` and the two shapes. The `camcraft-mcp` skill says how to change a lead shape.

body:
## What happens

Since #917, the STEP reader gives each solid of a file its own facets. Two closed solids that touch along a wall can put one mesh edge into 2k facets, k in each direction.

The branch of #917 (PR B, stacked on #2843) adds one rule in `crates/geometry/src/geometry/shared_edge.rs`, `solids_touch`. The slicer (`slice_bodies::closed_solids`) and the winding check (`pick/winding.rs`) use it. The rule passes such an edge when all of these are true:

- the count is even and balanced
- each body uses the edge one time in each direction
- no apex is on the edge line
- each body has a facet on the plane of a facet of a different body

The bodies come from a link over plain edges only (two uses, one in each direction).

The rule fixes the shipped `sample_ap214.step`: it slices, and it reads as outward for Align. Two cases stay open:

1. **A face whose full boundary is shared edges.** Example: two blocks stacked face to face. The contact face of each block links to no other facet of its block over a plain edge. Thus each shared edge sees four bodies that use it one time each, and the rule refuses. Align then refuses the model as non-manifold. The slicer refuses it by name.
2. **The feature graph** (`geometry::feature::features_of_facets`) has its own edge map. It does not use the rule. On `sample_ap214.step`, 216 tangent edge pieces pick apart (`no_pickable_edge_is_a_tangent_piece_of_a_longer_one_in_any_step_fixture`).

## Rules that were tried

- **Radial pairing** (pair each facet with its angular neighbour about the edge). It failed on the sample: the solids overlap, and two facets in the same direction lie on one plane, so the order is ambiguous. It also let two cubes that meet only along one line pass, which is wrong.
- **Wall on a wall** (`solids_touch`, kept). It fails in case 1, because the bodies form before the shared edges are judged.

## Safety

Neither case gives wrong toolpath output. Each is a refusal by name, or an edge that picks in pieces. The pins:

- `shared_face_bodies::welded_non_manifold_solids_are_refused_as_a_model_fault`
- `shared_face_bodies::the_sample_laid_flat_generates_3d_finish_and_pocket_with_no_gouge`

## Wanted

- Link a face that only shared edges bound to its own solid. For example, use the STEP solid ranges (`Mesh::solid_ranges`, `app::mesh_solids`) when the model has them, or pair the coplanar opposed facets first.
- Give the feature graph the same rule.
- Remove the known-fail markers that name this issue.

body:
## What happens

The solidcore STEP path (#917, PR B on `issue/917-solidcore-step`) meshes the four-turn thread flank fixture with too many facets.

The test is `crates/app/tests/import_step_thread.rs`, `a_four_turn_thread_flank_meshes_at_full_fidelity_in_a_bounded_count`.

| Reading | Main (old reader, #1602 division) | solidcore path |
|---|---|---|
| Facets | under 5000 (the pin passes on main) | 391338 |
| Chord | 5e-3 mm | 5e-3 mm requested, replanned at 2.5e-3 mm |
| Debug test time | not measured | 93 s |

The import note is: `STEP sheet #418: replanned at 2.5e-3 mm chord to meet the requested 5e-3 mm measured tolerance`.

## Cause

At the pinned rev, solidcore-tess plans the long, thin helicoid strip isotropically. The plan at a 5 um chord measures over the tolerance. The seam then replans at half the chord (`PLAN_MARGIN`), and the count goes up again. Our seam (`crates/kernel/src/machining_mesh.rs`, `planned`) can only pick the chord. It cannot pick the shape of the division.

## Options

1. An anisotropic plan upstream in solidcore-tess: divide along the strip by the curvature of each direction.
2. A division hint through our seam: pass a per-face step in u and v to the planner, if solidcore-tess gets an API for it.

## Acceptance

The pin `facets.len() < 5_000` in the test above passes, with the other asserts of the test (chord not reduced, longest edge, area, axial gap). Until then, the test has the known-fail marker with this issue number.

Refs #917

Found by the new Windows check (Windows 11, Git for Windows defaults: `core.autocrlf=true`), main 380c29b3c, `cargo xtask gate quick`.

## What happens

Git for Windows checks text files out with CRLF by default. `.gitattributes` pins `crates/app/tests/golden/**`, tester kits, examples and `*.sh` to LF, but not every fixture that tests compare byte for byte or parse. Four suites (17 tests) fail on such a checkout, each within a second:

| Suite | Reads | Pinned? |
|---|---|---|
| post `explain_fanuc_family`, `explain_remaining` | `crates/post/tests/golden/explain/*.nc` | **no** |
| app `wire_taper_angle` | `crates/app/tests/edm/wire-iso-fixture.mch` (include_str) | **no** |
| app `import_step_curve_guard` | `testdata/models/box.step` (include_str) | **no** |

Example: `fanuc_explain_golden_preserves_program` - left (generated) ends lines with `\n`, right (golden from the checkout) with `\r\n`; the content is otherwise identical.

## Fix

Pin every byte-compared or parsed text fixture to LF, e.g.:

```
crates/*/tests/golden/** text eol=lf
crates/*/tests/**/*.mch  text eol=lf
testdata/**/*.step       text eol=lf
testdata/**/*.stp        text eol=lf
```

(or one broader rule for `crates/*/tests/**` and `testdata/**`), then `git add --renormalize .`. A unit test in xtask (or a CI-free check) could assert that `git check-attr eol` is `lf` for every file under the golden/fixture dirs.

## Done means

On a fresh Windows checkout with `core.autocrlf=true`, the four suites above pass; `git check-attr eol -- <each fixture>` reports `lf`.

- The surface is a degree-3 B-spline surface with a strong twist.

- A STEP fixture that we made, with a strongly twisted degree-3 B-spline face, imports without the refusal. The fixture is not the user's file.

body: ### What are you trying to do I want to describe my own machine in the Machines pane, for example a 3-axis grblHAL mill with a 4th-axis rotary (A, about X) on the table. The file editor (machine_file_editor.rs) shows one field for each key the file already has (machine::fields). It cannot add an axis, remove one or change their order in kinematics.default.parts. Today I have to edit the .mch file in a text editor and reload it. ### How you imagine it working - One row per axis part, in chain order, under `table` or under `head` in `kinematics.default.parts`, with up, down and remove buttons and an "add axis" control. A linear part is `X`, `Y`, `Z` (and `U`, `V` for a wire machine); a rotary part is `A`, `B` or `C`. - A linear row edits `direction` (`1` / `-1`, #373). - A rotary row edits `axis` (±X, ±Y, ±Z, or three numbers for any other vector) and its travel, or none for continuous. - A rotary that turns the work also edits `nose_to_axis` and `axis_to_table` (#785), the two distances the clearance gates read. They are measurable with a rule or taken from the maker's data. - Under them, a collapsed "Kinematics" group holds `pivot` and `offset` (#1962). It is closed by default and open when the file already states a pivot. For a rotary under `head` (one that tilts the tool, like a B head), the group is open instead, since the two distances do not apply to it and the pivot is what places it. This issue only adds the group; #1970's rows fill it (see below). - The letter follows the `axis` by RS-274: about X is `A`, about Y is `B`, about Z is `C`. When `axis` is set, the editor suggests that letter. A row whose letter and `axis` disagree (an `A` about Y, say) shows a note at the row; whether that should also block a save is the validator's call, as now. - The edits go through `MachineDraft`, as `add_coolant` and `remove_coolant` do, so keys the editor does not know are kept. - The validator judges the result as now. A refusal shows at the row it concerns, and a save stays blocked while a refusal stands. - Moving a rotary changes its `parent` and `chain_order`, since the parser derives them from the nesting (#1962). Tests pin that, and that `pivot`, `offset`, `zero_offset`, `rollover` and `sign_convention` survive an add, a move and a remove. For illustration only, the axis list as it started to look in another CAM tool (solidcraft). It is a hint at the idea, not a layout to copy. Its `Pivot` row stands in the open; the proposal here puts the pivot in a collapsed group instead. **Overlap with #1970.** #1970 adds rows for the #1962 trunnion keys to `fields.rs` and `sheet.rs`, the same files and the same rotary row. This issue does not edit those keys; it only keeps them, and the rotary row's collapsed "Kinematics" group is where #1970's rows go. Its blockers (#1962, #1965, #1968) look done on `main`, so the two may run at the same time. Should this one wait for #1970, go first, or be folded into it? **A question before any code.** A rotary can be placed by `nose_to_axis` / `axis_to_table` (#785) or by `pivot` / `offset` (#1962). I do not see them as alternatives: the clearance gates read the #785 pair, the post's kinematics the #1962 pair, so a file may well want both. Hence the proposal above rather than a choice between them: a rotary that turns the work shows the two distances, with `pivot` / `offset` in a collapsed group; a rotary under `head` (one that tilts the tool, like a B head) shows the group open, since the two distances do not apply to it. Does that split work for you, or should the editor show both pairs alike? **And one about a machine with both.** `nose_to_axis` is measured with Z at `safe_retract`, and as I read it with the head straight. On a machine with a tilting head (B under `head`) and a rotary that turns the work (A under `table`), the nose moves away from that line as B tilts, so the one number no longer holds. Do the index-swing gates handle such a machine today? If not, should the editor still offer the two distances on its A, or say that they are judged only with the head straight? I would like to take this one if it is wanted.

body:
Filed by the maintainer in chat (2026-11-19): "I want to be able to type text, select a face and location for the text, text size and a tool and it does the engraving. It's common for people to want engraved part numbers but it isn't modeled."

## What the user wants

1. Type a text string, for example a part number `SN-0471`.
2. Pick the face to engrave and place the text on that face.
3. Set the text height and the tool.
4. CamCraft makes the engraving toolpath, verifies it and posts it.

## What exists today

- `OpType::Engrave` and `OpType::Trace` machine 2D geometry along the tool centreline. They obey the mark law (#1595): a shallow mark passes, a deep cut is refused.
- 2D geometry comes from a DXF sketch (the `Sketch` entity, #1862). Work to feed sketch chains to Engrave and Trace is #1869. SVG import is #1880.
- There is no way to make geometry by typing text. A user today must draw the letters in a CAD program, export a DXF, and import it.

## What to build

- A text-to-outline step: convert the typed string into glyph outlines as 2D regions (outer loop + hole loops for letters such as A, B, O). Use one of the fonts already bundled in `assets/ui/fonts/`; the outlines are the same vectors the UI draws. Flatten the glyph curves to polylines within the setup tolerance. Clean-room: only the font's own licensed outlines, no vendor letter shapes.
- An undoable command (for example `InsertText`): the text string, height, and the placement become a `Sketch` the operation kinds already read. Ship its MCP tool with it (#128 law).
- Placement: select a planar face (or the setup top plane) in the viewport, then set X/Y and rotation. The existing `sketch::face_frame` code gives the face frame.
- Parameters on the Engrave operation: text string, height (mm or inch through the unit lens), letter spacing, depth (bounded by the mark law), tool, feed, and climb. The toolpath path is the existing Engrave/Trace generator.
- Two ride modes later, both from the same outlines: ride the glyph boundary with a small end mill or v-bit, and single-line engraving on the glyph skeleton with a v-bit. Pick one for the first cut; record the choice in `docs/decisions/`.

## Suggested label triage

`enhancement`, `area:2d`, `P6`, `effort:high` (safety floor: new toolpath and posted G-code). The filing account has no label rights; a collaborator sets these.

## Done means

The user types a string, picks a face and a spot, sets a height and a tool, and CamCraft generates, verifies and posts an engraving toolpath. A golden test pins the CL output for a known string and font. The placement, `.camproj` round-trip and MCP tests pass.

body:
The maintainer asked for this work, in his own words (2026-11-18):

> issue; p4; there is shaded and wireframe today. There should be a shaded with no edges, and wireframe "see thru" as well.

## State of the code

The Browser pane has a "Solids" choice with two modes (`DisplayMode` in `crates/ui/src/state.rs`, radios in `crates/ui/src/egui_app/browser_pane.rs`):

- `ShadedEdges`: flat-shaded faces with the CAD wire over them. It is the default.
- `Wireframe`: faces go to the depth buffer only, so the model reads as a hidden-line drawing. Hidden edges do not show.

## Wanted

Four display modes:

1. **Shaded** (with edges). The current default. No change.
2. **Shaded, no edges.** Faces only. No CAD wire over them. Edges of a picked or hovered feature still show, so that picking stays visible.
3. **Wireframe** (hidden lines removed). The current mode. No change.
4. **Wireframe, see-through.** Every edge draws, front and back, with no hidden-line removal. The model does not hide the stock, the fixtures or the toolpath behind it. Hidden edges may draw in a lighter tone, so the front stays readable.

Details:
- The choice stays one control in the Browser pane. Four radios or one drop-down. Plain English labels: "Shaded", "Shaded, no edges", "Wireframe", "Wireframe, see-through". Tooltips say what each does.
- The mode is view state (a direct field flip, never a command), as today. It applies to the model, the stock and the fixtures in the same way. The toolpath and the simulation stock follow their own rules and stay readable in each mode.
- The setting is saved with the other view settings, if the others are saved. An old file without the field loads with the default.
- Picking works in each mode. In "Wireframe, see-through" a click picks the edge nearest to the cursor, front or back, with the nearest to the camera first. State the rule in the test.
- The renderer builds the edge and face passes once for each geometry change (precalculate and cache; frame target under 10 ms). No per-frame rebuild of the edge lists.

## Constraints

- A UI PR needs before and after screenshots of all four modes in the PR body. Tests assert labels, roles, which mode is selected, the state field and the picking rule. They do not assert pixels. Pixel snapshots are release-lane only and a PR never changes a PNG.
- Update the layout test of the Browser page. Keep each file under about 400 lines.
- `DisplayMode` is also used by the wasm build. The new modes must work there.

## Done means

- A test shows that each radio sets its mode and that the labels exist.
- A test shows the draw list for each mode: faces and edges as listed above.
- A test shows picking in "Wireframe, see-through" with the stated rule.
- The PR has the screenshots.

Depends on #1861 and #1862 (the `Sketch` entity placed on a stock, with the virtual model reference).

Scope:

1. Wire EDM 2-axis profile on DXF sketch chains: the user picks closed or open chains, and the side and the direction for each chain. The kerf (wire radius and spark gap) offset uses the same law as the model-based Wire EDM operation.

3. Laser: find out if a laser cut operation exists. If it exists, give it the same chain picking. If it does not exist, say so in a comment and file the issue for it. Do not add a laser operation in this issue.
4. The kerf verify law runs against the sketch chains. An offset that cannot fit (a slot narrower than the kerf, a self-crossing offset) refuses by name. It never posts a path that cuts on the wrong side.
5. The commands have their MCP tools, or a follow-up issue `MCP: <command>`.

title: Process changes - fork maintainers please subscribe

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: P?
labels.description: Paused: never picked until the maintainer sets a real priority

body:
**Subscribe to this issue** (the "Subscribe" button on the right) if you work from a fork of CamCraft, especially with an AI agent.

Forks sync product code only at release tags (AGENTS.md "A fork syncs from upstream at each cut tag"). But the *process* - `AGENTS.md`, the agent definitions in `.claude/agents/`, the skills in `.claude/skills/` and `scripts/gate.*` - changes between releases, and a fork's agents should follow the current rules (review labels, priority labels, release steps, and so on).

**How it works:**
- `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` holds one number. Every PR that changes a process file bumps it.
- Every such PR also adds a comment **here**: the new version, what changed, and what to pull. Subscribers get one notification per change.
- A fork's agent compares its `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` with upstream's at the start of each session and, if upstream is newer, pulls just the process files (AGENTS.md "Process files sync on every session"). Product code still waits for the next release tag.

**To pull by hand:**
```
git fetch upstream
git checkout upstream/main -- AGENTS.md .claude/agents .claude/skills .claude/PROCESS_VERSION scripts/gate.ps1 scripts/gate.sh
git commit -m "chore(process): sync process files to upstream PROCESS_VERSION <n>"
```

This issue stays open and pinned. It's labelled `P?` so no agent ever picks it up as work.
